newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Mar 27.

text.p: A threat by disgruntled National MP John Banks to quit the party if the privileges committee clears Deputy Winston Peters of charges assaulting him had the one-seat-majority coalition government on the back foot on Wednesday night. Banks' threat -- confirmed by National whip John Carter -- triggered speculation of a by-election in the Whangarei electorate. Page 1.

Members of Parliament questioned on Wednesday why maximum security prisoners were allowed to lift weights, potentially increasing ability for escape attempts. Labour's justice spokesman, Phil Goff, told the justice and law reform select committee he was amazed the most dangerous prisoners were given weight training. Page 1.

A Waitangi Tribunal ruled on Tuesday in favour of the 174,000-hectare Muriwhenua land claim and headed for a showdown with the government by threatening to force return of land to the far northern tribes. The tribunal has never used its
mandatory powers, which are restricted to return of state-owned enterprise and crown forestry assets. Page 2.

Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Wednesday admitted the coalition had had its "little challenges that have grabbed the headlines", but claimed it was far from the verge of collapse. Labour leader Helen Clark, however, said the government had been in trouble from the outset and forecast big coalition changes before the end of the three-year parliamentary term. Page 2.

The job of educating the public about compulsory superannuation before the September referendum would not be easy, Sir John Robertson, chairman of the newly-appointed independent panel for voter education, said on Wednesday. "It's a task which is very complex, which is on a short time scale ... naturally we are concerned about it." Page 2.
The size of the dole queue was questioned at a Parliamentary select committee on Wednesday when it was revealed that some people struck off the unemployment register were not working. Page 2.

Prudential Assurance was still keen to expand after swallowing NZI Life, the managing director of Prudential Australia and New Zealand, Trevor Perry, said on Wednesday. Prudential bought NZI Life from Scottish owner General Accident for $163.3 million, heading off other bidders touted to include Sir Ron Brierley's Guiness Peat Group and AMP. Perry said the Prudential buyout made Prudential a "clear third" in life companies measured by funds under management in New Zealand. Page 20.

Treasurer Winston Peters has been criticised by the National Bank for presenting a "fiscally irresponsible" budget policy statement. The statement, presented earlier this month, was based on "over-optimistic" economic projection, had no "safety net" of budget surpluses, and was not anchored by total government spending, National Bank chief economist Adrian Orr said. Peters said the National Bank is wrong on all counts. Page 20.

Merchant bank Grant Samuel's bid to act for Defiance Foods preference shareholders was "interference in the market" and "unjustified as well as unnecessary", Defiance Foods chairman Tom O'Brien said on Wednesday. Grant Samuel had written to preference shareholders offering to act for them in a pid to pry $3 a share out of Defiance as a result of the sale of Defiance's New Zealand milling and baking assets to Goodman Fielder. Page 20.

Comalco New Zealand slumped to a $13.5 million loss in 1996, a huge reversal from the previous year's $106.9 million profit, but the company says the outlook for this year is "reasonable". The $120 million earnings drop was due to a combination of weak international aluminium prices and higher operating costs in commissioning the $464 million upgrade of Tiwai Point aluminium smelter, Comalco managing director Kerry McDonald said on Wednesday. Page 20.

Progressive Enterprises made a sharp recovery in bottom-line profit to $8.01 million for the six months, from a depressed $2.21 million a year ago. However, the result issued on Tuesday was still down on the $10.53 million the comapny posted in the first half two years ago. The latest result was achieved through a "substantial improvement" in profits from the company's supermarkets and a reduction in costs. Georgie Pie continued to incur losses, the company said. Page 20.
